quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Dear Ms. Patel, thank you for applying for the office assistant job. We would like to invite you to an interview on Thursday at 10 a.m. Please bring a copy of your resume.
quests.question: Ms. Patel has already been offered the job.
quests.hint: Notice the action the email asks her to take.
quests.explanation: She is invited to an interview, so no job offer has been made yet.
quests.evidenceLine: We would like to invite you to an interview on Thursday at 10 a.m. Please bring a copy of your resume.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The art museum's new exhibition shows paintings from three different centuries. Visitors can join a guided tour at noon or explore on their own with a free audio guide. The exhibition is open until the end of October.
quests.question: Visitors must join a guided tour.
quests.hint: Is the tour the only way to see the exhibition?
quests.explanation: Visitors may also explore on their own with an audio guide.
quests.evidenceLine: Visitors can join a guided tour at noon or explore on their own with a free audio guide.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Meteorologists expect the temperature to drop below zero tonight. Drivers are advised to leave early tomorrow morning because the roads may be icy, and some buses could be delayed. Road crews have already spread salt on the main highways.
quests.question: Tomorrow morning's roads may be dangerous for drivers.
quests.hint: Consider the risk the weather brings to roads.
quests.explanation: The passage warns of icy roads, which are a risk for drivers.
quests.evidenceLine: Drivers are advised to leave early tomorrow morning because the roads may be icy, and some buses could be delayed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Kaya's Repair Shop fixes phones and tablets. Most repairs take about an hour, so customers can wait, but larger problems may take up to two days. The shop is on the ground floor of the old market building and opens at nine.
quests.question: Customers must leave their phones at the shop overnight.
quests.hint: Check what customers are free to do during most repairs.
quests.explanation: Most repairs take an hour and customers can wait, so leaving the phone overnight is not required.
quests.evidenceLine: Most repairs take about an hour, so customers can wait, but larger problems may take up to two days.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A password is safer when it is long and contains letters, numbers, and symbols. Using the same password for every account is risky because one leak can expose all of them. Many security experts also suggest changing important passwords twice a year.
quests.question: Using one password for all accounts is unsafe.
quests.hint: Read the sentence about reusing passwords.
quests.explanation: Reusing one password is risky because a single leak can expose every account.
quests.evidenceLine: Using the same password for every account is risky because one leak can expose all of them.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Vitamin C is found in oranges, peppers, and strawberries. Doctors say that eating fresh fruit and vegetables is the best way to get it, rather than relying only on pills. Fruit juice can help too, though it usually contains less fiber than whole fruit.
quests.question: Doctors think pills are the best source of vitamin C.
quests.hint: Look for the doctors' advice.
quests.explanation: Doctors prefer fresh fruit and vegetables over pills.
quests.evidenceLine: Doctors say that eating fresh fruit and vegetables is the best way to get it, rather than relying only on pills.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Sana was late for school on Monday because her bus broke down. Her teacher was not angry and let her join the class quietly, but Sana missed the first ten minutes. She apologized to the class and promised to leave home earlier the next day.
quests.question: Sana was late because she woke up late.
quests.hint: Why was Sana late?
quests.explanation: Her bus broke down. Waking up late is not mentioned.
quests.evidenceLine: Sana was late for school on Monday because her bus broke down.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Leila works as a tour guide in Cairo. She speaks Arabic, English, and French, and most customers ask her to lead the evening tours because the city is cooler then. The evening tours end with dinner at a small restaurant near the river.
quests.question: Leila speaks Arabic, English, and French.
quests.hint: Read the list of languages Leila speaks.
quests.explanation: Arabic, English, and French are all named as languages she speaks.
quests.evidenceLine: She speaks Arabic, English, and French, and most customers ask her to lead the evening tours because the city is cooler then.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The public swimming pool on King Road is open from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. It is busiest on Saturday mornings, when many families bring their children for lessons. Lifeguards are on duty during all opening hours.
quests.question: The pool closes at 6 p.m.
quests.hint: Find the closing time.
quests.explanation: The pool is open until 9 p.m., not 6 p.m.
quests.evidenceLine: The public swimming pool on King Road is open from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Video calls use more internet data than voice calls. Farid limits his calls to thirty minutes when he uses his phone plan, because he has only five gigabytes of data each month.
quests.question: Farid keeps his video calls short to save data.
quests.hint: Why does Farid limit his calls?
quests.explanation: He has a small monthly data limit, so short calls help him stay within it.
quests.evidenceLine: Farid limits his calls to thirty minutes when he uses his phone plan, because he has only five gigabytes of data each month.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Many supermarkets now sell fruit and vegetables without plastic wrapping. Customers put the food in paper bags or their own containers, which reduces the amount of waste. Some shops also give a small discount to customers who bring their own containers.
quests.question: Selling produce without plastic wrap helps reduce waste.
quests.hint: Read the result of skipping plastic wrapping.
quests.explanation: The passage says using paper bags or containers reduces waste.
quests.evidenceLine: Customers put the food in paper bags or their own containers, which reduces the amount of waste.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Regular exercise strengthens the heart and improves mood. Even a brisk walk of thirty minutes on most days can make a difference, according to many doctors. Doctors also recommend stretching, especially for people who sit at a desk all day.
quests.question: Doctors say a short walk has no effect on health.
quests.hint: Notice how many doctors describe walking.
quests.explanation: Doctors say even a thirty-minute brisk walk can make a difference.
quests.evidenceLine: Even a brisk walk of thirty minutes on most days can make a difference, according to many doctors.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In Spanish, adjectives usually come after the noun, as in "casa grande" for "big house." English is different because adjectives normally come before the noun. For example, Spanish speakers say "coche rojo," while English speakers say "red car."
quests.question: English puts its adjectives after the noun, just as Spanish does.
quests.hint: Compare English with Spanish.
quests.explanation: English adjectives normally come before the noun.
quests.evidenceLine: English is different because adjectives normally come before the noun.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Sushi is made with rice that is mixed with vinegar. Contrary to popular belief, it does not always contain raw fish, because vegetables and cooked seafood are common fillings too. Rolled sushi is often served with soy sauce, ginger, and a little green wasabi.
quests.question: Sushi cannot be made with vegetables.
quests.hint: Look at the fillings the passage lists.
quests.explanation: Vegetables are named as common sushi fillings.
quests.evidenceLine: Contrary to popular belief, it does not always contain raw fish, because vegetables and cooked seafood are common fillings too.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Fog forms when warm, wet air cools near the ground. In the valley where Amara lives, fog often covers the roads in the early morning and clears by ten o'clock. Drivers in the valley are advised to use their headlights until the fog has cleared.
quests.question: Morning fog in Amara's valley usually disappears by mid-morning.
quests.hint: Look at when the fog clears.
quests.explanation: Fog clears by ten o'clock, which is mid-morning.
quests.evidenceLine: In the valley where Amara lives, fog often covers the roads in the early morning and clears by ten o'clock.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Emeka started selling homemade jam at a weekend market five years ago. Today he supplies twelve local shops and has hired two assistants to help him make it. He plans to open a small shop of his own next year.
quests.question: Emeka now supplies twelve local shops and has two assistants.
quests.hint: Compare the business at the start with today.
quests.explanation: He began at a weekend market and now supplies twelve shops with two assistants.
quests.evidenceLine: Today he supplies twelve local shops and has hired two assistants to help him make it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Daniela keeps a small notebook where she writes her plans for the next day. She says planning at night helps her feel calm in the morning, and she has done it for three years.
quests.question: Daniela draws up her plan for the day at breakfast time.
quests.hint: When does Daniela make her plans?
quests.explanation: She plans at night, not in the morning.
quests.evidenceLine: She says planning at night helps her feel calm in the morning, and she has done it for three years.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Every summer, the town holds an open-air theater festival in the old castle yard. This year's festival features six plays, and tickets are cheaper for students and retired people. The castle yard can hold about four hundred people.
quests.question: Students can buy cheaper tickets to the festival.
quests.hint: Who pays less for tickets?
quests.explanation: Tickets are cheaper for students and retired people.
quests.evidenceLine: This year's festival features six plays, and tickets are cheaper for students and retired people.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Zainab joined a running club to prepare for a 10-kilometer race. The group meets three times a week, and every meeting includes a short warm-up and a longer run. The race will take place in the city park in October.
quests.question: The running club meets more than twice a week.
quests.hint: Count how often the club meets.
quests.explanation: Meeting three times a week is more than twice a week.
quests.evidenceLine: The group meets three times a week, and every meeting includes a short warm-up and a longer run.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Building a bookshelf takes about three hours if you follow the instructions. Hector finished his in two hours because he had built the same kind before. The bookshelf is made of pine and has five shelves.
quests.question: Hector took longer than three hours to build his bookshelf.
quests.hint: Compare Hector's time with the usual time.
quests.explanation: He finished in two hours, which is faster than the usual three.
quests.evidenceLine: Hector finished his in two hours because he had built the same kind before.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no wind or weather there. Footprints left by astronauts can last for millions of years because nothing moves them. Scientists are studying these footprints to learn how the Moon's dust behaves.
quests.question: Astronauts' footprints on the Moon are blown away by wind.
quests.hint: Is there any wind on the Moon?
quests.explanation: The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no wind to move footprints.
quests.evidenceLine: The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no wind or weather there.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Emperor penguins huddle together in large groups to stay warm during Antarctic storms. They take turns standing on the outside of the group, where it is coldest. The huddle slowly moves, so every bird gets a chance to stand in the warmer center.
quests.question: Penguins take turns in the coldest part of the group.
quests.hint: Who stands on the outside?
quests.explanation: The birds rotate to the outer edge, where it is coldest.
quests.evidenceLine: They take turns standing on the outside of the group, where it is coldest.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Before clocks were common, people in villages told the time by the sun and the church bell. Trains later made it necessary to use standard times, because schedules needed to be the same in every town.
quests.question: Railway schedules created a need for standard time.
quests.hint: Look for the reason standard times became necessary.
quests.explanation: Trains needed schedules that matched in every town.
quests.evidenceLine: Trains later made it necessary to use standard times, because schedules needed to be the same in every town.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Cactus plants store water in their thick stems. This allows them to survive in the desert, where it may not rain for many months. Their sharp spines also protect them from animals that might eat them.
quests.question: Cactus plants keep water stored in their thick stems.
quests.hint: Think about what the stem stores.
quests.explanation: The passage says cactus plants store water in their thick stems.
quests.evidenceLine: Cactus plants store water in their thick stems. This allows them to survive in the desert, where it may not rain for many months.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The radio show "Morning Talk" is broadcast at 9 a.m. from Monday to Friday. On Saturdays, a music program is played in the same time slot. Listeners can also hear the show again online later in the day.
quests.question: On Saturdays, listeners can also hear "Morning Talk" at 9 a.m.
quests.hint: Check the Saturday slot at 9 a.m.
quests.explanation: A music program takes that slot on Saturdays.
quests.evidenceLine: On Saturdays, a music program is played in the same time slot.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Fire drills at Riverside Office happen twice a year. When the alarm rings, employees must leave by the stairs and must not use the elevators. A manager checks that everyone has reached the parking lot before people go back inside.
quests.question: Employees should take the elevator during a fire drill.
quests.hint: Read the rule about elevators.
quests.explanation: Employees must use the stairs and avoid elevators.
quests.evidenceLine: When the alarm rings, employees must leave by the stairs and must not use the elevators.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In Mexico, families celebrate the Day of the Dead by decorating altars with photos, flowers, and favorite foods of relatives who have passed away. It is a joyful occasion rather than a sad one.
quests.question: The celebration is meant to be happy rather than sad.
quests.hint: Look at how the passage describes the mood.
quests.explanation: The passage calls it a joyful occasion.
quests.evidenceLine: It is a joyful occasion rather than a sad one.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Jamila wants to buy a laptop that costs $600, and she has decided not to use a credit card. She has already saved $250 and puts aside $70 each month from her salary.
quests.question: Jamila still needs $350 to pay for the laptop.
quests.hint: Subtract her savings from the price.
quests.explanation: $600 minus $250 leaves $350.
quests.evidenceLine: Jamila wants to buy a laptop that costs $600, and she has decided not to use a credit card. She has already saved $250 and puts aside $70 each month from her salary.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The bus from the airport to the city center runs every twenty minutes. The trip lasts forty minutes, so a passenger who catches the 9:00 bus will arrive at 9:40. Tickets can be bought from the driver or from a machine at the station.
quests.question: A passenger on the 9:20 bus will reach the city center at 10:00.
quests.hint: Add the trip time to the departure time.
quests.explanation: A 9:20 departure plus forty minutes is 10:00.
quests.evidenceLine: The trip lasts forty minutes, so a passenger who catches the 9:00 bus will arrive at 9:40.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Kwame has a big family with three sisters and one brother. He is the second oldest child, and his youngest sister was born the year he started school. The whole family gathers at his grandmother's house every New Year.
quests.question: Kwame has no younger brothers or sisters.
quests.hint: Look at Kwame's position among the children.
quests.explanation: His youngest sister was born the year he started school, so he does have a younger sibling.
quests.evidenceLine: He is the second oldest child, and his youngest sister was born the year he started school.
